data.falsifier: ci run from a parent-adopted tree as another agent reports the tree HEAD after the fix

data.question: Why does ci run check the parent's commit?

evidence.note: research note CONFIRMED; regression test fails unfixed

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts exactly the pre-fix symptom the change claims to remove, so it cannot be the regression test for B0c245a07a1. The intent says the bug is that "a subagent standing in a foreign worktree checks the parent's HEAD and the ci gate is not attributed to its own item", and that the fix makes `ci run` resolve the ref via `called_from` so the run lands on the subagent's own item. This test invokes the CLI as a subagent (`agent="sub"`) from inside the worktree, and then asserts `body["sha"] == primary` — `primary = _git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")`, i.e. the parent/primary repo's HEAD, not the worktree's — and `assert "recorded" not in body`, i.e. the gate is *not* attributed to the run's item. Both assertions are precisely the two failure modes named in the bug description ("checks the parent's HEAD", "not attributed to its own item"). Given the fixed code resolves via `called_from` (the worktree it is called from, as the sibling test and the existing MCP test with `called_from=tree` both assert `sha == tree HEAD`), the fixed `ci run` should return the worktree's HEAD and record to the item owning it; this test would then fail on the fixed code (and, as written, encodes the behaviour that must be gone). Concretely: with `--agent sub` and `cwd=tree`, after the fix `body["sha"]` is `_git(tree, "rev-parse", "HEAD")` (the "parent work" commit), not `primary`, and `body` contains `recorded`, so both asserts fail. The only way this test passes is if the CLI still falls back to the parent/primary HEAD and skips attribution — the bug itself. Note also that the sibling `test_ci_run_with_repo_from_a_worktree_still_checks_that_trees_head` exercises the non-subagent path, where cwd and `called_from` coincide, so it passes on the unfixed code as well; combined with the inversion above, nothing in this diff actually fails before the fix and passes after it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_gate.py:test_ci_run_in_a_foreign_worktree_checks_the_primarys_head

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test asserts the *pre-fix* outcome that the bug report calls the defect. It sets up a subagent (`agent="sub"`) sitting in the worktree `tree` and then asserts `body["sha"] == primary` (the primary repo's HEAD) plus `"recorded" not in body` (lines asserting `assert body["sha"] == primary` / `assert "recorded" not in body`). Those are exactly the two symptoms named in the intent: "a subagent standing in a foreign worktree checks the parent's HEAD and the ci gate is not attributed to its own item". The fix is supposed to resolve the ref from `Ctx.called_from` "like the MCP path", and the MCP path is pinned by the pre-existing test immediately above (`A.ci_tool(repo, action="run", called_from=tree)` → `res.data["sha"] == _git(tree, "rev-parse", "HEAD")`): a call attributed to `tree` must report `tree`'s HEAD, not the primary's. Consequently this test cannot be a regression test for B0c245a07a1: if the unfixed `head_here_or_repo(cwd)` really returned the worktree's HEAD (so the test fails before the fix as required), then the fixed, `called_from`-based CLI must also return the worktree's HEAD and record the run against T1 — making this test fail *after* the fix. If instead the unfixed code already produced the primary's HEAD, the test passes before and after and demonstrates nothing. Note the sibling test in the same hunk (`test_ci_run_with_repo_from_a_worktree_still_checks_that_trees_head`, same `_item_with_ci` setup, same `_cli_in(tree, repo)` invocation) asserts the opposite result — `body["sha"] == _git(tree, ...)` and `body["recorded"]["item"] == "T1"` — for a run from the same directory, which underscores that the assertion above encodes the un-fixed behaviour. This violates the project rule that a bug fix must carry a regression test that fails on the unfixed code [D-rules-hierarchy].
